key_insight: Deep generative crystal-structure predictors are useful, but most of their apparent gains come from learning prototype families rather than discovering truly new structures.
engineering_relevance: For computational materials design, this means CSP benchmarking should prioritize prototype-independent recovery, not just top-1 accuracy against known libraries.
method: Benchmarked 12 representative generative CSP models across latent-variable, diffusion, flow-matching, autoregressive, and manifold random-walk designs.
Used identical structure-matching, symmetry, and consensus criteria to compare all methods fairly against TCSP 2.0.
Performed a controlled prototype-removal retraining test on the strongest model to measure dependence on training-set prototypes.
evidence_signal: On 180 test structures (and a leakage-controlled subset of 46), template retrieval reached 68.3% top-1 success, while the best generative methods were close behind; most generative hits overlapped with template substitution results.
watch_item: High benchmark scores can overstate novelty because performance drops sharply when prototype families are removed, so leakage control and prototype-aware evaluation are essential.
paper_title: Deep Generative Crystal Structure Prediction: A Benchmark Study and a Controlled Test of Prototype Dependence
